description:
Problem: the owner requires the local and CI reviews to be literally the same code, differing only where the execution environment forces it. Today CI orchestration lives in about 20 gated steps of .github/workflows/oracle-verdict.yml (select, scans, isolation, loop, finalize, redact, guard, posts, uploads, dispatch), with if: chains acting as a second decision layer, while the local path re-implements most of it in local.py.

Prior art: the single-job decision record (_project/decisions/oracle-single-review-job-2026-10-25.md) and the existing cli.py subcommands; this item extends them into one entrypoint rather than adding a parallel layer.

Outcome: one driver with phase entrypoints (for example cli.py review prepare, attempts, finalize, publish, and sweep) runs a fixed sequence: trusted inputs, plan, classify, pre-scan, harness ensure (pin file), isolation check, attempts, post-scan, finalize and judge, redact, record and post (status, review or comment, retry state), gate dispatch. It runs through an environment adapter interface covering PR context, change source, credential client, classifier key source, isolation capability, scan roots, result sink, state store and harness binary. The CI adapter supplies GitHub event context and sinks. Each phase is its own workflow step holding only its own secrets: prepare (plan, classify with TYPESAFE_API_KEY, pre-scan), then attempts (gateway token only), then finalize (post-scan, finalize, redact), then the App-token mint, then publish; phases pass state through files. oracle-verdict.yml keeps only environment-forced steps (checkouts, provisioning, tailnet join, App-token mint, artifact upload) and one step per driver phase; the sweep job calls a driver subcommand. The reviewer stays self-contained behind this entrypoint and one pinned config, so the planned split into a separate project is a move (owner Q11).

Decision gates:
1. Characterise first: on develop, capture plan, final, status and comment outputs for a fixture matrix (first review, follow-up, carry, dispute, fork, draft, oversize, absence, integrity error, App missing) as golden tests that pass on develop; the refactor must pass them unchanged.
2. Secrets stay step-scoped: no phase receives a secret it does not use. Leak test: during an attempt, read /proc/<pid>/environ of every reviewer ancestor up to the runner and assert no classifier key, App token or App private key; os.environ checks do not count. The gateway token and URL stay readable in the attempts phase (owner accepted this residual on 2026-10-26).
3. Isolation checks stay fail-closed in CI.
4. Delivery in two PRs (owner Q10, live proof before cutover): PR 1 adds the driver phases as a non-posting shadow after the existing posting steps, reusing the existing loop's attempt outputs (it never starts a reviewer or spends model quota), and uploads its outputs; record five live runs whose shadow plan, final, status and comment equal the posted ones. PR 2 cuts over and deletes the replaced steps. Any mismatch stops the cutover.
5. If any behaviour cannot move without changing outcomes, stop and report (Q10 lifted the 'no CI change' guardrail for the caller, not for behaviour).

Item guardrails: no change to policy, selection, the decision rule, budgets or the gate; no new workflow permissions.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. Never use git stash (refs/stash is shared across worktrees). Commit as Joe Harris <joeharris76@gmail.com>, staging explicit paths only; no git add -A, no --no-verify, no SKIP, no agent trailers. Durable text (commits, PR bodies, docs, code) carries no tracker ids, session labels or plan references. Maintained code has no explanatory comments or docstrings (make comment-policy-check). Before publishing run make docs-reference-inventory-check, make doc-contracts-guard and make pr-preflight, and self-review with the code review action, fixing every Critical and Required finding. Publish only with make pr-open: never gh pr create, a raw push-and-open, or a PR-body override line; if make pr-open refuses, stop and report the exact refusal instead of routing around it. Until oracle-omp-pin-single-source-20261026 merges, make pr-open may run only with PATH prefixed by the darwin-arm64 omp 18.12.1 build recorded in that item (SHA-256 fa41b27d434380e99b713e4f9ced0f73eb1fc0c409fdf23a57c119971d24bac5, from https://build.stencil.so/d/omp/20261017-231446-291e055/omp-darwin-arm64), verified with shasum immediately before use; never any other side-loaded omp. Close out only with oracle SHIP on the exact head, every oracle thread answered (reply naming the fixing SHA, then resolve) and make pr-arm; never raw gh pr merge or a ruleset or settings change, and never a stand-in, adjudication or backoff reset unless the owner names the PR and head (and the finding) in the current request after an Owner instruction comment. Never edit, delete, dismiss or minimise an oracle review, review comment or commit status, and never post a commit status by hand. Run /oracle-review only on a pending or absent head, or after a Dispute: reply with file:line counter-evidence; never to re-roll a decided head. Do not close, reopen, rerun or rebase other PRs. Until oracle-gateway-cloud-builder-access-20261025 merges, publish only from the owner's Mac. Rollback: if a change to the verdict or gate workflows or to the local review breaks its first live run after merge in a way that blocks other PRs, stop, run make trunk-revert PR=<n>, and report to the owner, who chooses between an absence stand-in and the broken-oracle-gate procedure. Never print tokens, keys, or the gateway URL or hostname; never spend model quota outside the review harness. Owner decisions are recorded in context and in the decisions file; a step that would contradict one stops and asks the owner.
